==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|he'p}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|hĕlp}} * {{IPA|en|/hɛlp/|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-help.wav|a=Southern England}} ** {{audio|en|en-uk-to help.ogg|a=UK|text=to help}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-help.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|[hɛo̯p]|~|[hɛʊ̯p]|a=UK,l-vocalisation}} * {{IPA|en|/help/|a=AU,NZ}} ** {{IPA|en|[he̝o̯p]|~|[he̝ʊ̯p]|a=NZ,l-vocalisation}} * {{enPR|hĕp|a=Southern US,AAVE,dated}}, {{IPA|en|/hɛp/}}{{R:Hall PGSMS|3|2|88}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛlp|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:help>}} From {{inh|en|enm|help}}, from {{inh|en|ang|help|t=help, aid, assistance, relief}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*helpō|t=help}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hilpiz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hulpiz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱelb-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*ḱelp-|t=to help}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Hälpe|t=help}}, {{cog|fy|help|t=help}}, {{cog|cim|hölfe|t=help}}, {{cog|nl|hulp|t=help}}, {{cog|de|Hilfe|t=help, aid, assistance}}, {{cog|lb|Hëllef|t=help}}, {{cog|mhn|hilf|t=help}}, {{cog|wym|hyłf|t=help}}, {{cog|yi|הילף|t=help}}, {{cog|da|hjælp|t=help}}, {{cog|fo,is|hjálp|t=help}}, {{cog|nb|hjelp|t=help}}, {{cog|nn|hjelp}}, {{m|nn|hjølp|t=help}}, {{cog|sv|hjälp|t=help}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|-|s}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} Action given to provide [[assistance]]; [[aid]]. #: {{ux|en|I need some '''help''' with my homework.}} # Something or someone which provides assistance with a task. #: {{ux|en|He was a great '''help''' to me when I was moving house.}} # {{lb|en|computing}} [[documentation|Documentation]] provided with [[computer]] [[software]] that could be accessed using the computer. #: {{ux|en|I can't find anything in the '''help''' about rotating an image.}} # {{lb|en|countable}} A [[study aid]]. #: {{ux|en|I've printed out a list of math '''helps'''.}} #* {{quote-web|en|year= c. 2002|title=Scripture Study Helps|url=https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/manual/new-testament-teacher-resource-manual/scripture-study-helps|site=The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints|text=In 1979 the Church published a Latter-day Saint edition of the King James Version of the Bible in English. Included in this edition were numerous '''helps''' to make a study of the scriptures more meaningful and rewarding.}} # {{lb|en|usually|uncountable}} One or more people employed to help in the maintenance of a house or the operation of a farm or enterprise. #: {{ux|en|The '''help''' is coming round this morning to clean.}} #: {{ux|en|Most of the hired '''help''' is seasonal, for the harvest.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} Correction of deficits, as by psychological counseling or medication or social support or remedial training. #: {{ux|en|His suicide attempts were a cry for '''help'''.}} #: {{ux|en|He really needs '''help''' in handling customer complaints.}} #: {{ux|en|“He’s a real road-rager.” / “Yup, he really needs '''help''', maybe anger management.”}} =====Usage notes===== * The sense “people employed to help in the maintenance of a house” is usually an uncountable [[mass noun]]. A countable form — “a hired help”, “two hired helps” — is attested, but now less common. ''[[helper|Helper]]'' could be used if no more specific noun is available. =====Quotations===== {{see citations|en}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|action given to provide assistance}} {{l|en|aid}}, Cognate with {{cog|frr|halep}}, {{m|frr|heelpe}}, {{m|frr|help|t=to help}}, {{cog|stq| hälpe|t=to help}}, {{cog|fy|helpe|t=to help}}, {{cog|cim|hölfan|t=to help}}, {{cog|nl|helpen|t=to help}}, {{cog|de|helfen|t=to help}}, {{cog|nds|helpen}}, {{m|nds|hölpen}}, {{m|nds|hülpen|t=to help}}, {{cog|lb|hëllefen|t=to help}}, {{cog|yi|העלפֿן|t=to help}}, {{cog|da|hjælpe|t=to help}}, {{cog|fo,is|hjálpa|t=to help}}, {{cog|nb|hjelpe|t=to help}}, {{cog|nn|hjelpa}}, {{m|cog|hjelpe|t=to help}}, {{cog|sv|hjälpa|t=to help}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐌹𐌻𐍀𐌰𐌽|t=to help}}, {{cog|lt|šelpti|t=to help, support}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|+,holp|+,holpen}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide [[assistance]] to (someone or something). #: {{syn|en|see through}} #: {{ux|en|He '''helped''' his grandfather cook breakfast.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=76 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21579801-making-sense-statistics-riddle-our-days-snakes-and-ladders Snakes and ladders] |passage=Risk is everywhere.{{...}}For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you. “The Norm Chronicles”{{...}}aims to '''help''' data-phobes find their way through this blizzard of risks.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To assist (a person) in getting something, especially food or drink at table; used with ''to''. #: {{ux|en|It is polite to '''help''' your guests to food before serving yourself.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Help''' yourself to whatever's in the fridge.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To contribute in some way to. #: {{ux|en|The white paint on the walls '''helps''' make the room look brighter.}} #: {{ux|en|If you want to get a job, it '''helps''' to have some prior experience.}} #: {{ux|en|I've already taken three pills, but they don't seem to '''help''' my headache.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To provide assistance. #: {{ux|en|She was struggling with the groceries, so I offered to '''help'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Please, '''help'''!}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=19|passage=As soon as Julia returned with a constable, Timothy, who was on the point of exhaustion, prepared to give over to him gratefully. The newcomer turned out to be a powerful youngster, fully trained and eager to '''help''', and he stripped off his tunic at once.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=72–3 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/science-and-technology/21580133-how-microbes-promote-liver-cancer-overweight-punch-gut A punch in the gut] |passage=Mostly, the microbiome is beneficial. It '''helps''' with digestion and enables people to extract a lot more calories from their food than would otherwise be possible. Research over the past few years, however, has implicated it in diseases from atherosclerosis to asthma to autism.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[avoid]]; to [[prevent]]; to [[refrain]] from; to [[restrain]] (oneself). Usually used in nonassertive contexts with ''[[can]]''. #: {{ux|en|We couldn’t '''help''' noticing that you were late.}} #: {{ux|en|We couldn’t '''help''' but notice that you were late.}} #: {{ux|en|She’s trying not to smile, but she can’t '''help''' herself.}} #: {{ux|en|Can I '''help''' it if I'm so beautiful?}} #: {{ux|en|Can I '''help''' it that I fell in love with you?}} #: {{ux|en|Are they going to beat us? Not if I can '''''help''''' it!}} #: {{ux|en|She never does more than she can '''help'''.}} # {{lb|en|Hong Kong|Singapore}} To do something on the [[behalf]] of someone.{{cite-book|year=2012|chapter=7|author=Tony T.N. Hung|editors=Ee-Ling Low, Azirah Hashim|publisher=John Benjamins Publishing Company|title=English in Southeast Asia: Features, policy and language in use|text=In HKE, the implication is usually to do something on behalf of someone, and not just to assist someone in doing it. For example, when someone asks you “Can you help me wash the dishes?”, the expectation is that you will do it for (rather than with) that person.|page=126}} #: {{ux|en|Can you '''help''' me buy some groceries?|footer=Underlying meaning is “Can you go do the groceries for me?”}} # {{lb|en|Singapore|Singlish|imperative}} To [[assist]] or [[sympathize]] with (the speaker); {{n-g|used to express [[displeasure]], [[disappointment]] or [[exasperation]].}} #: Compare {{ncog|ms|tolong|t=help; please}} and {{ncog|nan-hbl|導郎|tr=tō͘-lông|t=help; please}} #: {{co|en|'''Help''' {{l|en|lah|id=attitude}}.|Give me a break.|inline=1}} =====Usage notes===== * Use 4 is often used in the [[imperative mood]] as a call for assistance. * In uses 1, 2, 3 and 4, this is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the ''to infinitive''. It can also take the bare infinitive with no change in meaning. * In use 5, [[can't help]] is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the ''gerund (-ing)'' or, with but, the bare infinitive. * For more
